n_sec4: Pakistani law (section 4) applied: the children of a son or daughter who died first took their parent's share.
n_mushtaraka: Mushtaraka case: the full brothers share the third with the maternal half-siblings (Shafi'i, Maliki).
n_akdariyya: Akdariyya case: the well-known ruling of Zayd ibn Thabit.
n_zayd: Grandfather with brothers: he takes a brother's share, a third or a sixth, whichever is more (Zayd ibn Thabit).
n_radd: Radd: what was left after the fixed shares was returned to the same sharers (not to the husband or wife).
n_raddSpouseAeh: There is no other relative, so the rest was also returned to the husband or wife (the view of Ibn Taymiyyah, which Ahl-e-Hadith scholars follow). Scholars differ on this: ask a mufti before acting.
n_raddSpouse: There is no other relative, so the husband or wife also took the rest (the fatwa of the later Hanafi scholars).
n_dhawi: Dhawu al-arham: no sharer or residuary is left, so relatives through women inherit. Their division is disputed: confirm with a mufti.
n_unassigned: Part of the estate has no heir in this list. Ask a mufti.
n_imam: Ja'fari fiqh: a wife alone takes a quarter; the rest is the Imam's right. Ask your marja's office.
n_hajib: Ja'fari fiqh: the father is alive, so the brothers and sisters reduced the mother's share.
n_class3: Ja'fari fiqh, third class: confirm the division among paternal and maternal uncles and aunts with your marja's office.
n_awl: Awl: the fixed shares came to more than the estate, so every share was reduced in the same proportion.
n_landWife: Ja'fari fiqh: a wife takes no share of the land itself, only of the value of buildings and trees. Her share in a house is from the value of the building.
why_husband: Husband: a half, or a quarter with children
why_wife: Wife: a quarter, or an eighth with children (wives share it)
why_mother: Mother: a third, or a sixth with children or two brothers or sisters
why_daughters: Daughters: a half for one, two thirds for two or more
why_sondaughter: Son's daughter: a sixth with one daughter
why_children: Children: all the rest, a son twice a daughter
why_maalGhayr: Sisters with daughters take the rest
why_sisters: Sisters: a half for one, two thirds for two or more
why_consSister: Paternal half-sister: a sixth with a full sister
why_rep: Share of a parent who died first
why_passed: Died first: share to their children
b_twoDaughters: Two daughters have taken the full two thirds
b_twoSisters: Two full sisters have taken the full two thirds
b_higherAsaba: A closer relative takes the rest
b_notSharer: Not an heir while closer heirs exist
b_nothingLeft: Nothing is left after the fixed shares
b_diedBefore: Died first, so not an heir
b_parentAlive: Their own father or mother is alive
b_class1: Excluded by the first class (parents, children)
b_class2: Excluded by the second class (brothers and sisters, grandparents)
b_fullSibling: Excluded by full brothers or sisters
n_raddLater: The original position of the Shafi'i and Maliki schools is that the remainder goes to the public treasury (bayt al-mal); here the fatwa of later jurists is used, which returns it to the sharers or gives it to the dhawu al-arham.
n_baitulmal: In this school the remainder is not returned to the husband or wife (no radd); it belongs to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). Ask a mufti before acting.
